commands.name: Intelligence and Attack Surface
commands.mission: Build a continuously versioned, evidence-backed model of reachable assets, identities, technologies, dependencies, and likely attack paths.
commands.inputs: Business-service priorities; legal scope; asset inventories; threat intelligence; approved public and customer-provided data.
commands.outputs: Target graph; asset and identity inventory; confidence-tagged hypotheses; collection gaps; prioritized entry paths.
commands.collaboration: Campaign Engineering; Identity and Trust; Cloud; Network; Software Supply Chain; Mission Architecture.
commands.boundary: Discovery does not imply permission to interact with an asset. Active validation requires a scope token and the appropriate action tier.

commands.name: Human and Physical Access
commands.mission: Evaluate authorized human, collaboration, facility, and device-mediated access pathways without causing coercion, harassment, or uncontrolled physical risk.
commands.inputs: Approved personas and populations; facility boundaries; communication channels; pretext constraints; emergency contacts.
commands.outputs: Interaction records; control-bypass evidence; exposure patterns; training and process improvements; physical access findings.
commands.collaboration: Identity and Trust; Campaign Engineering; Windows/Microsoft Cloud; Mobile; Independent Control.
commands.boundary: No test may target uninformed third parties, create real financial or reputational harm, or exceed the written human/physical rules of engagement.

commands.name: Identity and Trust
commands.mission: Assess authentication, authorization, federation, credential lifecycle, session integrity, and trust relationships across human and workload identities.
commands.inputs: Identity architecture; federation metadata; test accounts; entitlement data; trust diagrams; recovery workflows.
commands.outputs: Identity path analysis; trust-boundary findings; token and session evidence; entitlement risk; corrective design guidance.
commands.collaboration: Windows/Microsoft Cloud; Cloud; Web; API; Cryptography; Cross-Surface Patterns.
commands.boundary: Kerberos here covers protocol and trust semantics; the Windows command owns AD implementation and path abuse. PKI here covers authentication use; Cryptography owns validation and primitive assurance.

commands.name: Campaign Engineering and Adversary Emulation
commands.mission: Integrate validated capabilities into coherent, threat-informed campaigns that measure prevention, detection, response, and mission resilience.
commands.inputs: Threat scenarios; target graph; approved objectives; capability availability; blue-team measurement goals.
commands.outputs: Campaign graph; emulation plan; infrastructure design; stage results; replay package; detection opportunities.
commands.collaboration: All maneuver groups; Mission Operations; Independent Control; Purple Team; Evidence and Assurance.
commands.boundary: Operational security and telemetry tradecraft apply to approved adversary infrastructure. Technical impact emulation requires explicit Control approval.

commands.name: Web and Browser
commands.mission: Assess server-side and browser-side web behavior, HTTP edge semantics, content handling, framework implementation, and route-level enforcement.
commands.inputs: Application inventory; routes; test accounts; architecture; proxy and CDN configuration; client code.
commands.outputs: Reproducible web findings; browser traces; server-edge differentials; route authorization evidence; remediation tests.
commands.collaboration: API; Identity; Business Logic; Data Systems; Network; Cross-Surface Patterns.
commands.boundary: Web authorization covers route and UI enforcement. API owns object/function enforcement. Web proxy/CDN work covers HTTP edge and cache semantics; Network owns routing and TLS termination.

commands.name: API, Integration and Service Interface
commands.mission: Assess machine interfaces, interface contracts, gateway behavior, object/function/property authorization, and trust transitions between services and partners.
commands.inputs: OpenAPI or interface schemas; gateway and mesh configuration; test identities; partner workflows; callback endpoints.
commands.outputs: Interface findings; authorization matrices; schema differentials; resource-abuse evidence; downstream trust analysis.
commands.collaboration: Web; Identity; Business Logic; Data; Containers; Cloud; Cross-Surface Patterns.
commands.boundary: API authorization owns object and function enforcement. Service-mesh scope is interface trust semantics; the Containers command owns Kubernetes traffic-plane configuration and reachability.

commands.name: Data Systems and Middleware
commands.mission: Assess storage, query, messaging, analytics, orchestration, backup, and database privilege boundaries across structured and unstructured data systems.
commands.inputs: Data-flow diagrams; test datasets; platform configurations; database roles; backup and replication topology.
commands.outputs: Data-path findings; privilege evidence; integrity and isolation tests; query/resource impacts; recovery-control observations.
commands.collaboration: Web; API; Cloud; Business Logic; Software Supply Chain; Cross-Surface Patterns.
commands.boundary: Production data access follows minimum-necessary rules; destructive statements, bulk extraction, and integrity-affecting tests require elevated approval or synthetic replicas.

commands.name: Mobile and Thick Client
commands.mission: Assess mobile and desktop client code, local trust, platform controls, IPC, storage, distribution, anti-tamper, and backend interaction.
commands.inputs: Application packages; symbols; test devices; build configuration; MDM policy; backend accounts and endpoints.
commands.outputs: Static and dynamic findings; platform-control bypass evidence; storage and transport findings; client/backend trust analysis.
commands.collaboration: API; Identity; Web; Software Supply Chain; Embedded; Cryptography.
commands.boundary: Device compromise is permitted only on designated test devices. Native desktop and Electron clients sit here; server-side services remain with Web/API.

commands.name: Business Logic, Fraud and Economic Abuse
commands.mission: Model and test stateful workflows, economic invariants, ownership, incentives, fraud controls, and abuse paths that scanners cannot infer.
commands.inputs: Workflow models; product rules; ledgers; roles; fraud controls; test balances; legal and customer-impact constraints.
commands.outputs: Broken-invariant evidence; abuse graphs; quantified economic exposure; control gaps; safe replay scenarios.
commands.collaboration: Web; API; Identity; Data; Distributed Ledger; Assurance.
commands.boundary: Business races cover transactional and economic effects; Cross-Surface Patterns owns generic concurrency and TOCTOU mechanisms.

commands.name: Distributed Ledger and Smart Contract
commands.mission: Assess on-chain code, economic mechanisms, cross-chain trust, wallets, nodes, consensus, governance, and supporting off-chain infrastructure.
commands.inputs: Source and bytecode; deployment manifests; protocol economics; wallet flows; oracle and bridge architecture; test networks.
commands.outputs: Contract and protocol findings; economic simulations; chain traces; invariant violations; remediation and fork-replay tests.
commands.collaboration: Business Logic; Cryptography; API; Software Supply Chain; Exploit Engineering.
commands.boundary: No mainnet value movement or governance action without explicit case-specific authorization; use local forks and testnets by default.

commands.name: Windows, Active Directory and Microsoft Cloud
commands.mission: Assess Windows endpoints and servers, Active Directory, Microsoft cloud identity and collaboration, management planes, and enterprise lateral paths.
commands.inputs: Forest and tenant architecture; test accounts; endpoint inventory; trust and management topology; collaboration configuration.
commands.outputs: Privilege and lateral paths; endpoint evidence; tenant findings; trust and synchronization risks; detection opportunities.
commands.collaboration: Identity; Network; Cloud; Campaign Engineering; Software Supply Chain; Legacy Enterprise.
commands.boundary: Kerberos here is AD implementation and path abuse; Identity owns protocol/trust semantics. Collaboration scope includes Microsoft 365 and Office clients.

commands.name: Linux, macOS and Open Systems
commands.mission: Assess Unix-like endpoints and servers, kernel and userland privilege boundaries, persistence, local credentials, platform policy, and remote administration.

commands.outputs: Local and remote privilege findings; persistence evidence; platform-control gaps; cleanup record; hardening guidance.
commands.collaboration: Network; Cloud; Containers; Campaign Engineering; Exploit Engineering; Software Supply Chain.
commands.boundary: Kernel research is shared with Exploit Engineering; this command owns target-platform configuration, integration, persistence, and operational validation.

commands.name: Network, Wireless and Telecom
commands.mission: Assess network control and data planes, routing, segmentation, infrastructure appliances, wireless and telecom protocols, and network-mediated trust.

commands.outputs: Reachability and segmentation findings; protocol evidence; appliance risks; covert-channel observations; topology corrections.
commands.collaboration: Intelligence; Cloud; Windows; OT; Embedded; Web; Campaign Engineering.
commands.boundary: Network-layer ADC/CDN scope covers routing and TLS termination; Web owns HTTP edge/cache semantics. Radio transmission follows spectrum and safety authorization.

commands.name: Cloud Provider and SaaS Control Plane
commands.mission: Assess cloud and SaaS control planes, organizational policy, identities, managed services, resource boundaries, guardrails, and post-compromise paths.

commands.outputs: Control-plane findings; identity and resource paths; guardrail gaps; service-specific evidence; cloud-native remediation tests.
commands.collaboration: Identity; Containers; Network; Data; Windows/Microsoft Cloud; Software Supply Chain; Cryptography.
commands.boundary: Cloud KMS coverage is control-plane abuse; Cryptography owns primitive and key-lifecycle assurance. Provider policies can be narrower than contractual scope.

commands.mission: Assess container artifacts, runtimes, Kubernetes control and traffic planes, workload isolation, cluster policy, registries, and event-driven compute.

commands.collaboration: Cloud; Software Supply Chain; API; Linux; Exploit Engineering; Cryptography.

commands.collaboration: Windows; Linux; Network; Data; Cloud; Campaign Engineering; Independent Control.
commands.boundary: Potentially fragile or unsupported systems default to passive review, configuration assessment, emulation, or replica testing.

commands.outputs: Source-to-artifact paths; pipeline findings; provenance gaps; secret exposure; package and release remediation tests.
commands.collaboration: Containers; Cloud; Web/API; Exploit Engineering; Cryptography; Windows/Linux.
commands.boundary: GitOps here covers source, build, provenance and release. Containers owns cluster-runtime consumption. Never publish test packages to public ecosystems.

commands.collaboration: Exploit Engineering; Cryptography; Network/Wireless; OT; Software Supply Chain; Mobile.
commands.boundary: Embedded side-channel specialists examine physical hardware leakage. Cryptography owns cryptographic implementation leakage; Cross-Surface Patterns owns software-observable discrepancies.

commands.name: OT, ICS and Cyber-Physical
commands.mission: Assess industrial control and safety-critical environments through process-aware, consequence-limited testing that protects life, environment, equipment, and continuity.
commands.inputs: Zones and conduits; process and hazard models; approved windows; operator contacts; digital twins or replicas; recovery procedures.
commands.outputs: Cyber-to-process paths; safety-control observations; protocol and engineering-station findings; validated detection and recovery improvements.
commands.collaboration: Network; Embedded; Windows/Linux; Campaign Engineering; Independent Control; Purple Team.
commands.boundary: No generic IT operator independently executes potentially disruptive tests on physical processes. Safety and process owners can stop activity immediately.

commands.name: AI, ML, GenAI and Agentic Systems

commands.collaboration: Web/API; Data; Software Supply Chain; Identity; Cloud; Cross-Surface Patterns; Cryptography.

commands.outputs: Root-cause analysis; minimized proofs; reliability data; exploit primitives; mitigation analysis; coordinated disclosure package.

commands.boundary: PKI here covers validation; Identity covers certificate authentication. HSM/KMS here covers primitives and key lifecycle; Cloud covers control-plane abuse.

commands.outputs: Reusable pattern library; root-cause mappings; variant-search plans; cross-domain attack paths; test-case improvements.
commands.collaboration: Every command; Knowledge Graph; Exploit Engineering; Evidence and Assurance.
commands.boundary: Authorization-pattern research is generic; Web/API/Identity own platform enforcement. Generic concurrency/TOCTOU lives here; Business Logic owns transactional effects.

commands.inputs: Firmware images; update bundles; hardware inventory; schematics where available; debug access; attestation evidence; isolated lab targets; recovery images.
commands.outputs: Platform-trust findings; firmware and peripheral attack paths; isolation evidence; impact bounds; restoration and remediation guidance.
commands.collaboration: Embedded and IoT; Exploit Engineering; Cryptography; Cloud; AI; Software Supply Chain; Independent Control and Assurance.
commands.boundary: Firmware writes, DMA tests, controller resets, and accelerator disruption require explicit target authority, recovery proof, monitoring, and an independent stop path.

commands.name: Transportation, Space and Clinical Systems
commands.mission: Assess connected transportation, space, navigation, autonomous, medical, and clinical systems with consequence-aware and human-safety controls.
commands.inputs: System and safety architecture; asset and protocol inventories; process hazards; operator contacts; simulators or digital twins; maintenance and restoration procedures.
commands.outputs: Cross-domain attack paths; safety and availability observations; protocol findings; bounded impact evidence; restoration and resilience guidance.
commands.collaboration: OT and ICS; Embedded and IoT; Network and Telecom; Identity; Cloud; Cryptography; Independent Control and Assurance.
commands.boundary: No live action may risk life, clinical care, navigation, transport safety, public infrastructure, or irreversible equipment impact. Simulation, passive evidence, and operator-supervised validation take precedence.
